gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 accepts solar only inside a 12–60 V, 20 A window (1,000 W max), or that its box holds no solar charging cable. A buyer adding BLUETTI's own 200 W panels must wire them in a way that stays under 60 V and 20 A. This matters most for the 3×200 W panel pack BLUETTI sells alongside it, which BLUETTI's own page does not fit-check against the station.
standout_why: I compared against backuppowerhub.com home-backup and fridge-backup pages and EnergySage (cited). Backuppowerhub lists the Elite 200 V2 only as '1,000W solar, not expandable, no 240V' and gives no panel Voc window or connector for any model. EnergySage gives only maximum solar watts and says to 'stay within the unit's voltage and wattage limits' without stating them. None gives the 12–60 V / 20 A window or the missing cable. I did not score it 3 because I could not open a maker page for the panel's open-circuit voltage, so the series/parallel arithmetic that would decide the panel count is unsourced.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W continuous). Its PV input is 12–60 V / 20 A / 1,000 W max per BLUETTI's US page, so any panel set must stay under 60 V and 20 A. Not expandable and no 240 V (per backuppowerhub), so it suits fridge-and-essentials backup, not panel-wired whole-home.

Solar panels: 2× BLUETTI 200 W Portable Solar Panel (SP200L, MC4 leads). BLUETTI's own kit pairs exactly two with the Elite 200 V2. I avoid the 3-panel pack because I could not confirm from a BLUETTI page that three fit the 60 V / 20 A window.
Solar charging cable: required, because BLUETTI's in-the-box list for the Elite 200 V2 has no solar cable. I could not confirm which connector the station uses, so the exact cable is unconfirmed.
